extraction.name: Visual Genome
extraction.description: A dataset of images densely annotated with region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, scene graphs, and question-answer pairs to support comprehensive scene understanding.
extraction.creator: Ranjay Krishna; Yuke Zhu; Oliver Groth; Justin Johnson; Kenji Hata; Joshua Kravitz; Stephanie Chen; Yannis Kalantidis; Li-Jia Li; David A. Shamma; Michael S. Bernstein; Li Fei-Fei
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected and verified entirely through crowdsourcing on Amazon Mechanical Turk. Workers created region descriptions with bounding boxes, extracted objects and their boxes, added attributes and relationships to form region graphs, merged them into scene graphs, and wrote freeform and region-based question-answer pairs. All annotations then went through verification.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, User-generated content data, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some descriptions like "it is a sunny day" do not contain any objects and therefore have no region graphs associated with them. Workers are asked to not generate any graphs for such descriptions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the intersection of YFCC100M and MS-COCO; annotations consist of freeform worker-generated texts and image-localized boxes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: 6 months of collection after 15 months of experimentation and iteration
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs were canonicalized to WordNet synsets using Stanford NLP tools, heuristic rules, and worker verification; scene graphs were formed by merging co-referenced objects across region graphs based on overlap and worker confirmation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Descriptions were filtered for diversity using BLEU-score thresholds against prior image-specific and global descriptions; workers were required to draw bounding boxes satisfying coverage and quality constraints; descriptions without explicit objects produced no region graphs; annotations were verified by majority voting or rapid judgments.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Workers on AMT drew bounding boxes and wrote region descriptions, extracted objects from descriptions and grounded them with boxes, added attributes and relationships from text to create region graphs, confirmed object co-reference for scene graphs, and wrote both freeform and region-based QA pairs under specified rules.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotations were verified using majority voting by three workers for most components and rapid judgments for objects; an annotation was kept if at least two of three workers marked it correct.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 verifiers per annotation; approximately 50 region descriptions per image; 8 freeform QA pairs per image task and around 20 region-based pairs
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 33,000 unique AMT workers; 93.02% from the United States, with smaller proportions from the Philippines, Kenya, India, Russia, and Canada; majority aged 25-34; 54.15% male and 45.85% female.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Stanford dependency parser; Stanford NLP tools
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The paper states that this is the "first release" of the Visual Genome dataset and describes the data collection as an "ongoing effort of collecting this dataset," but it does not provide explicit versioning timeframe, maintainers for future releases, or deprecation policies.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support next-generation computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, enabling applications such as image search, question answering, and robotic interactions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is somewhat biased toward images of people and certain sports-related content; worker geography is heavily skewed toward the United States.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Canonicalization mappings are imperfect and still contain ambiguity; some descriptions contain no explicit objects and therefore have no region graphs; current baseline models perform poorly on several tasks, indicating the difficulty of the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and benchmarking computer vision models for comprehensive scene understanding, including object and attribute prediction, relationship prediction, dense image captioning, visual question answering, semantic image retrieval, and image understanding evaluation.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We map all objects, attributes, relationships, and noun phrases in region descriptions and QAs to synsets in WordNet... rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: When a worker writes a new description, we programmatically enforce that it has not been repeated by using BLEU score thresholds set to 0.7... Finally, we ask workers to draw bounding boxes that satisfy one requirement: coverage... Quality requires that each bounding box be as tight as possible... Some descriptions like "it is a sunny day" do not contain any objects and therefore have no region graphs associated with them... All Visual Genome data go through a verification stage as soon as they are annotated.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: When a new image is added to the crowdsourcing pipeline with no annotations, it is sent to a worker who is asked to draw three bounding boxes and write three descriptions for the region enclosed by each box... Each description is sent to one crowd worker, who extracts all the objects from the description and grounds each object as a bounding box in the image... we present each worker with a region description along with its extracted objects and ask them to add attributes to objects or to connect pairs of objects with relationships... To create question answer (QA) pairs, we ask the AMT workers to write pairs of questions and answers about an image.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) as our primary source of annotations.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: Verification is conducted using two separate strategies: majority voting (Snow et al., 2008) and rapid judgments (Krishna et al., 2016). All components of the dataset except objects are verified using majority voting... An annotation is added to our dataset if at least two (a majority) out of the three workers verify that it is correct.
